speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have yellowish discoloration of your skin and eyes, which suggests jaundice; can you tell me if you have experienced any recent fever, abdominal pain, or changes in your urine and stool color? Additionally, have you recently consumed any new medications, supplements, or alcohol?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and recent recreational drug use, have you experienced any flu-like symptoms such as fever, muscle aches, or severe fatigue in the last few weeks? Also, have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools?

REQUEST TEST: Liver function panel (ALT, AST, ALP, Bilirubin, Albumin, INR)
REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A, B, and C serology
REQUEST TEST: HIV antigen/antibody test

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver function panel (ALT: 650 IU/L, AST: 600 IU/L, Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL, INR: 1.5); Hepatitis A, B, and C serology: Not detected in provided data; HIV antigen/antibody test: Not detected in provided data.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is highly unlikely given your severe jaundice and agitation; appendicitis does not cause yellowing of the skin. Your recent drug use and sexual history raise serious concern for viral hepatitis, HIV, or acute hepatitis A. Please confirm if you have noticed dark urine or pale stools, and await the results of the liver panel and serology I have ordered.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis (suspected Hepatitis A or B)
